intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn to introduce yourself in English: your name, where you're from, your job and the things you like. You'll also learn what to say when someone introduces themselves to you. Warm-up: can you say your name and your city in English?
teachingNotes: Build a short introduction in a fixed order: greeting → name (Hi, I'm Rina / My name is Rina) → where you're from (I'm from Bandung / I'm from Indonesia / I'm Indonesian) → job (I'm a nurse. I work in a hospital.) → likes (I love cooking.). Accept I'm and I am, My name is and My name's. Learners without a job can say I'm a student or I'm a homemaker.

Common errors from Indonesian: *'I'm from Indonesian' (after from comes the country: I'm from Indonesia; the nationality goes without from: I'm Indonesian); *'I teacher' / *'I'm teacher' (Saya guru → I'm a teacher: keep am and a/an); *'I am work in a bank' (work is already the verb, so no am: I work in a bank); *'Introduce, my name is…' (word-by-word 'Perkenalkan': just say Hi, I'm… or, formally, Let me introduce myself).

Likes reuse the like lesson: like / love + a noun (I like music) or + verb-ing (I love cooking); My hobby is + -ing (*'My hobby is cook'); My hobbies are… (hobbies = more than one, so are). Indonesian 'saya sangat suka' gives *'I very like': correct it to I really like… or I like… very much.

Responding: Nice to meet you. → Nice to meet you too. / You too. Then say your own name, show interest (Oh, nice! / Really? / Me too!) and ask one question back (What do you do? Where do you work? Do you like…? And you?). 'Saya juga' is Me too, not *'I also' or *'I too'. 'I'm fine, thanks' answers How are you?, not Nice to meet you. If you speak first, say Nice to meet you without too.

Register: Hi, I'm Budi with classmates and friends; Good morning. My name is Budi Santoso in an interview or a formal meeting. Nice to meet you is for the first meeting only; with people you already know, say Nice to see you (again). films (British) = movies (American).

Limits (A1): present only (to be, simple present, like + -ing, fixed questions). No past simple (avoid 'I was born in…', 'I studied…'), no future forms, no present perfect ('I've lived here for…'), no 'interested in'. Keep introductions to 3–5 short sentences.

keyPoints.title: Name, origin and job
keyPoints.explanation: Say your name with I'm … or My name is …. Say where you're from with I'm from + a city or country (I'm from Indonesia), or say your nationality without from (I'm Indonesian). Never 'I'm from Indonesian'. Say your job with I'm a/an + job, and where you work with I work in + place (no am before work).

examples.id: Hai, saya Rina. Saya dari Bandung.

examples.en: I'm a nurse. I work in a hospital.
examples.id: Saya perawat. Saya bekerja di rumah sakit.

examples.id: Selamat pagi. Nama saya Budi Santoso.

id.title: Nama, asal dan pekerjaan
id.explanation: Sebut namamu dengan I'm … atau My name is …. Sebut asalmu dengan I'm from + kota atau negara (I'm from Indonesia), atau sebut kebangsaanmu tanpa from (I'm Indonesian). Jangan pernah 'I'm from Indonesian'. Sebut pekerjaanmu dengan I'm a/an + pekerjaan, dan tempat kerjamu dengan I work in + tempat (tanpa am sebelum work).

keyPoints.title: Likes and interests
keyPoints.explanation: Say what you like with like / love + a thing (I like music) or + verb-ing for an activity (I love cooking). You can also say My hobby is + -ing (My hobby is reading), My hobbies are … for more than one, or In my free time, I + verb. Indonesian 'sangat suka' is I really like or I like … very much, not 'I very like'.

examples.id: Saya suka sekali memasak masakan Padang.

examples.en: In my free time, I play badminton.
examples.id: Di waktu luang, saya bermain bulu tangkis.

id.title: Hal yang disukai dan minat
id.explanation: Sebut apa yang kamu suka dengan like / love + benda (I like music) atau + kata kerja-ing untuk kegiatan (I love cooking). Kamu juga bisa bilang My hobby is + -ing (My hobby is reading), My hobbies are … untuk lebih dari satu hobi, atau In my free time, I + kata kerja. 'Sangat suka' dalam bahasa Inggris adalah I really like atau I like … very much, bukan 'I very like'.

keyPoints.title: Responding to an introduction
keyPoints.explanation: When someone says Nice to meet you, answer Nice to meet you too (or You too) and say your name. Then show interest (Oh, nice! / Really? / Me too!) and ask one short question back: What do you do? Where do you work? Do you like …? Or just: And you?

id.title: Menanggapi perkenalan

material.title: Name, where you're from and your job

blocks.text:
A short introduction has a simple order: **greeting → name → where you're from → job**.
- Name: **I'm** Rina. / **My name is** Rina. (*I'm* is the short form of *I am*.)
- From: **I'm from** Bandung. / **I'm from** Indonesia. Or say your **nationality** (*kebangsaan*, the word for a person from that country): **I'm Indonesian**.
- Job: **I'm a** nurse. / **I'm an** accountant. (*an* before a vowel sound, like *a, e, i, o, u*.)
- Where you work: **I work in** an office / a hospital / a shop.

With friends and classmates, **Hi, I'm Rina** is perfect. In an interview or a formal meeting, say **Good morning. My name is** + your full name.

id.text:
Perkenalan singkat punya urutan sederhana: **salam → nama → asal → pekerjaan**.
- Nama: **I'm** Rina. / **My name is** Rina. (*I'm* adalah bentuk pendek dari *I am*.)
- Asal: **I'm from** Bandung. / **I'm from** Indonesia. Atau sebut **kebangsaanmu** (*nationality*, kata untuk orang dari negara itu): **I'm Indonesian**.
- Pekerjaan: **I'm a** nurse. / **I'm an** accountant. (*an* sebelum bunyi vokal, seperti *a, e, i, o, u*.)
- Tempat kerja: **I work in** an office / a hospital / a shop.

Dengan teman dan teman sekelas, **Hi, I'm Rina** sudah pas. Di wawancara kerja atau rapat formal, bilang **Good morning. My name is** + nama lengkapmu.

blocks.text:
Four traps when you translate word by word:
- *Saya dari Indonesia* → **I'm from Indonesia**, not `I'm from Indonesian`. After **from** comes the **country** (a place). **Indonesian** is for a person, without *from*: *I'm Indonesian*.
- *Saya perawat* → **I'm a nurse**. Indonesian has no word for *am* and no *a*, but English needs both before a job.
- *Saya bekerja di kantor* → **I work in an office**, not `I am work in an office`. **work** is already the **verb** (the action word), so you don't add *am*.
- *Perkenalkan, nama saya Budi* → just **Hi, I'm Budi** or **My name is Budi**. Not `Introduce, my name is Budi`. (Very formal: *Let me introduce myself.*)

id.text:
Empat jebakan kalau menerjemahkan kata per kata:
- *Saya dari Indonesia* → **I'm from Indonesia**, bukan `I'm from Indonesian`. Setelah **from** ditulis **negaranya** (tempat). **Indonesian** untuk orang, tanpa *from*: *I'm Indonesian*.
- *Saya perawat* → **I'm a nurse**. Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya kata untuk *am* dan tidak pakai *a*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh keduanya sebelum pekerjaan.
- *Saya bekerja di kantor* → **I work in an office**, bukan `I am work in an office`. **work** sudah merupakan **kata kerja** (kata untuk aksi), jadi tidak perlu ditambah *am*.
- *Perkenalkan, nama saya Budi* → cukup **Hi, I'm Budi** atau **My name is Budi**. Bukan `Introduce, my name is Budi`. (Sangat formal: *Let me introduce myself.*)

blocks.prompt: Dimas is a driver in Jakarta. Which sentence is correct?
blocks.explain: work is the verb, so you don't need am: I work in Jakarta. 'I am work' and 'I working' are mistakes.

id.prompt: Dimas sopir di Jakarta. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: work adalah kata kerja, jadi tidak perlu am: I work in Jakarta. 'I am work' dan 'I working' itu salah.

blocks.text:
After your job, add one or two things you like. Use what you learnt in the lesson about like:
- **like / love + a thing**: I like **music**. I love **coffee**.
- **like / love + verb-ing** (an activity): I love **cooking**. I like **watching** films.
- **My hobby is + -ing**: My hobby is **reading**. More than one hobby: **My hobbies are** …
- **In my free time, I + verb**: In my free time, I **play** badminton.

id.text:
Setelah pekerjaan, tambahkan satu atau dua hal yang kamu suka. Pakai yang sudah kamu pelajari di pelajaran tentang like:
- **like / love + benda**: I like **music**. I love **coffee**.
- **like / love + kata kerja-ing** (kegiatan): I love **cooking**. I like **watching** films.
- **My hobby is + -ing**: My hobby is **reading**. Lebih dari satu hobi: **My hobbies are** …
- **In my free time, I + kata kerja**: In my free time, I **play** badminton.

blocks.text:
Three Indonesian traps:
- *Saya sangat suka musik* → **I really like music** or **I like music very much**. Not `I very like music`: *very* can't go before *like*.
- *Hobi saya memasak* → **My hobby is cooking**, not `My hobby is cook`. *Memasak* doesn't change in Indonesian, but English needs **-ing** for an activity.
- **hobby** = one, **hobbies** = more than one (y becomes ies). One hobby **is**, more hobbies **are**.

id.text:
Tiga jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- *Saya sangat suka musik* → **I really like music** atau **I like music very much**. Bukan `I very like music`: *very* tidak bisa diletakkan sebelum *like*.
- *Hobi saya memasak* → **My hobby is cooking**, bukan `My hobby is cook`. Kata *memasak* tidak berubah dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **-ing** untuk kegiatan.
- **hobby** = satu, **hobbies** = lebih dari satu (y menjadi ies). Satu hobi pakai **is**, beberapa hobi pakai **are**.

blocks.explain: really goes before like: I really like swimming. very can't go before like or before the activity. You can also say I like swimming very much.

id.explain: really diletakkan sebelum like: I really like swimming. very tidak bisa diletakkan sebelum like atau sebelum kegiatannya. Kamu juga bisa bilang I like swimming very much.

blocks.text:
When someone tells you about themselves, reply in three small parts:
- **Reply and say your name**: *Nice to meet you.* → **Nice to meet you too.** (or just **You too.**) I'm Sari. If **you** speak first, say *Nice to meet you* without *too*.
- **Show interest**: **Oh, nice!** / **Really?** / **Me too!** (*saya juga*)
- **Ask one question back**: **What do you do?** (= what's your job?) **Where do you work?** **Do you like …?** Or just **And you?**

id.text:
Saat seseorang bercerita tentang dirinya, tanggapi dalam tiga bagian kecil:
- **Balas dan sebut namamu**: *Nice to meet you.* → **Nice to meet you too.** (atau cukup **You too.**) I'm Sari. Kalau **kamu** yang bicara duluan, bilang *Nice to meet you* tanpa *too*.
- **Tunjukkan minat**: **Oh, nice!** / **Really?** / **Me too!** (*saya juga*)
- **Ajukan satu pertanyaan balik**: **What do you do?** (= apa pekerjaanmu?) **Where do you work?** **Do you like …?** Atau cukup **And you?**

blocks.text:
- *Saya juga!* → **Me too!**, not `I also` or `I too`.
- Don't answer *Nice to meet you* with `I'm fine, thanks`: that is the answer to *How are you?*.
- **Nice to meet you** is only for the first time you meet someone. With people you already know, say **Nice to see you** (again).

id.text:
- *Saya juga!* → **Me too!**, bukan `I also` atau `I too`.
- Jangan jawab *Nice to meet you* dengan `I'm fine, thanks`: itu jawaban untuk *How are you?*.
- **Nice to meet you** hanya untuk pertama kali bertemu seseorang. Dengan orang yang sudah kamu kenal, bilang **Nice to see you** (again).

blocks.prompt: Sari: 'I'm from Bali. And you?' Which answer is best?
blocks.explain: And you? asks the same question back: where are you from? Answer with I'm from + place. 'I'm Bogor' says you are a city, and 'Yes, I'm from' has no place.

id.prompt: Sari: 'I'm from Bali. And you?' Jawaban mana yang paling tepat?
id.explain: And you? menanyakan hal yang sama balik: kamu dari mana? Jawab dengan I'm from + tempat. 'I'm Bogor' artinya kamu adalah sebuah kota, dan 'Yes, I'm from' tidak menyebut tempatnya.

blocks.text: Rina starts a new job at an office in Jakarta. Read how she meets Dimas. Look for the name, where they're from, their jobs and what they like, and how they reply to each other.

id.text: Rina mulai bekerja di kantor baru di Jakarta. Baca bagaimana dia berkenalan dengan Dimas. Perhatikan nama, asal, pekerjaan, dan hal yang mereka suka, serta cara mereka saling menanggapi.

blocks.text: Dimas says **Nice to meet you** first, so Rina adds **too**. Each person says one or two short things and then asks back (*And you?*). Short, simple sentences are perfect for a first meeting.

id.text: Dimas bilang **Nice to meet you** duluan, jadi Rina menambahkan **too**. Masing-masing bilang satu atau dua hal pendek, lalu bertanya balik (*And you?*). Kalimat pendek dan sederhana sudah pas untuk pertemuan pertama.
